findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks 'sender' field
findings.body: The expression `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` will raise a `KeyError` if the integration's metadata does not contain a `"sender"` key. The `build_integration` method only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, so integrations created before this change (or from webhook payloads missing the sender field) will not have this key. This code path is reached when an Integration exists but has no OrganizationIntegration (e.g., a stale integration from a previously deleted org-integration). The result is an unhandled 500 error instead of the intended graceful error page. A guard such as `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` should be used, and if it's missing, the request should be rejected with the error page.

findings.title: redirect_uri is not percent-encoded in the OAuth authorize URL
findings.body: The `redirect_uri` value (e.g., `http://testserver/extensions/github/setup/`) is interpolated directly into the query string without URL-encoding. Per RFC 6749 §3.1.2, the redirect_uri parameter value must be percent-encoded when included in the authorization request. Characters like `:`, `/` in the URI can cause parsing ambiguity with certain HTTP clients, proxies, or if GitHub tightens their parsing. Use `urllib.parse.quote(redirect_uri, safe='')` or `urlencode` to properly encode the parameter.

findings.title: Pipeline state fetch may return None, leading to confusing comparison semantics
findings.body: `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` can return `None` if the pipeline state has expired or was never set (e.g., user opens the GitHubInstallation step URL directly without going through OAuthLoginView). While the comparison `None != some_login` would correctly evaluate to True and return an error, if the metadata also lacks `"sender"` (see the KeyError issue above), the combination produces a 500 rather than a clear rejection. An explicit None-check with an early error return would make the intent clearer and avoid relying on the downstream KeyError as an implicit guard.

findings.title: Exception from safe_urlopen is not caught, could produce a 500
findings.body: If `safe_urlopen` raises an unexpected exception (e.g., a DNS resolution failure that propagates despite the 'safe' wrapper, or a misconfigured URL causing a ValueError), it will not be caught by the `try/except` block that only wraps `safe_urlread`. This would result in an unhandled 500 error during the OAuth token exchange step. Wrapping the entire token exchange (lines 423–429) in the try/except would make the error handling more robust.

findings.title: No test for the case where integration metadata is missing 'sender' key
findings.body: The test suite covers the happy path (sender matches) and the mismatch path (sender differs), but does not test the scenario where `integration.metadata` has no `"sender"` key at all. This is the case that triggers the KeyError bug on line 503 of the integration file. A test that creates an Integration without sender metadata and verifies a graceful error response (rather than a 500) would catch this regression.
